> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **2** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 96e724475c476d018c2b6d13dcd117ade14d0aa0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `4519e4ce745df42d23e801734bc34cd2189a0f45` — the merge of head `5cb34e77dc619f0bbed84983d96e127652f73136` into base `96e724475c476d018c2b6d13dcd117ade14d0aa0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 4519e4ce745df42d23e801734bc34cd2189a0f45 && git checkout 4519e4ce745df42d23e801734bc34cd2189a0f45
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 96e724475c476d018c2b6d13dcd117ade14d0aa0 5cb34e77dc619f0bbed84983d96e127652f73136 && git checkout -B drift-repro 96e724475c476d018c2b6d13dcd117ade14d0aa0 && git merge --no-ff 5cb34e77dc619f0bbed84983d96e127652f73136

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 96e724475c476d018c2b6d13dcd117ade14d0aa0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 96e724475c476d018c2b6d13dcd117ade14d0aa0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2ce8ceafbb22226656d94e6e0ecdd8e25c29301e`
Local-runs: probe — a node one-liner over `sdui.manifest.json` at `origin/main` (107 components) to count the declaring components of the 11 keys; objectui cloned at `db11afd4967c` and its `SDUI_BASE_PROPS` region diffed byte-for-byte against the branch. No repo gate family rerun.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Ported list byte-faithful — RIGHT. Branch `validate.ts:144-169` vs objectui `validate.ts:137` at `db11afd4967c`: the only differing line is the dropped `export`. All 20 names, both scopes and every `tsType` match.
2. Every-node accept-set change — RIGHT. `validate.ts:216` skips `bind`, `hidden`, `visibleWhen`, `hiddenOn`, `testId`; 0 of 107 manifest components declare any of them.
3. Where-undeclared guard — RIGHT. `validate.ts:220` (`!byName.has(key)`): a declared key falls through to the pre-PR `byName.get(key)` path (`:240`) with the same diagnostics and severities; `missing-required-prop` (`:203-211`) is untouched.
4. Public surface — WRONG by omission. `codegen.ts:41-50` (unchanged) emits a hand-kept `SduiBaseProps` via the public `generateDts` (`index.ts:24`). After this PR the validator accepts the five new keys while the generated types still refuse them, which is the drift objectui#11044 fixed (objectui `codegen.ts:13-32`, `:95-110`). The branch docblock `validate.ts:133-138` states "objectstack's `codegen.ts` emits no base-props interface": FALSE.
5. Changeset — IMPRECISE/FALSE in parts: "where the protocol declares them" is unresolvable for a consumer and wrong for the six; "newly accepted as an error" is meaningless; "served manifest" is unnamed, and the no-error-lost claim is manifest-relative (a consumer manifest declaring one of the five with an enum arm would lose an error); "module-local here" and "`codegen.ts` is unchanged" are internal notes, and the second hides the item-4 fact.
6. Tests — mostly prove the claims; the `type` case (`base-props-one-list.test.ts:42`) passes vacuously via `unknown-component`. Nothing pins `generateDts` to the list.

### ② Semver level

Measured on the tracked `sdui.manifest.json` (107 components): only `unknown-prop` warnings disappear, and `compile().ok` is unchanged. `patch` with `Clause-②: no` is consistent for that manifest; the changeset must scope the claim to it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Vanished worktree, redone: no bearing; the one-commit head was verified directly.
- Gate count 52 vs 54 in the PR body: no bearing on the contract.
- Two report comments against a budget of one: a process breach. The first report's false "codegen.ts has no base-props list" became the premise of the narrowed scope, and that premise is shipped in the docblock.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20578-sdui-base-props-port`
Reviewed-by: `session_01VDtqoecgES7ScQYGbFVDRv`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

Required fixes:
1. `validate.ts:133-138`: correct the LOCKSTEP paragraph.
2. Resolve the validator/codegen drift: emit `SduiBaseProps` from `SDUI_BASE_PROPS` with `Omit` for declared base attributes (objectui `codegen.ts:13-32`, `:95-110`), with a test pinning the emitted interface to the list.
3. Changeset: state the precise rule; "newly accepted"; name the measured manifest and scope the claim; drop the internal notes, keeping "no new export".
4. Test `:42`: give the `type` case a real subject or drop it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5cb34e77dc619f0bbed84983d96e127652f73136`
Local-runs: probe — objectui cloned at `db11afd4967c` and its `codegen.ts`, `validate.ts` and `html-tier-manifest-10735.test.ts` diffed byte-for-byte against the branch files; one node one-liner over `sdui.manifest.json` at `origin/main` (107 components) listing every declared input named as one of the 19 attribute members. No repo gate family rerun.

### ① Derived judgments

1. Prior FAIL fix 1 (LOCKSTEP paragraph): done, and true. `validate.ts:133-138` now names both consumers and the export-for-codegen-only. The list and Sets at `:139-178` and the skip at `:216-220` are byte-equal to objectui `validate.ts:137-173` / `:213` at the pin.
2. Prior FAIL fix 2 (codegen): done, and byte-faithful. `codegen.ts:22-25`, `:32`, `:61` and `:79-109` are equal to objectui `codegen.ts:13-32` / `:80-110`. The pin test is at `base-props-one-list.test.ts:65-83`. The `html-tier-manifest.test.ts:127` expectation is character-equal to objectui `html-tier-manifest-10735.test.ts:114`.
3. Prior FAIL fix 3 (changeset): done; every sentence is true. The no-error-lost claim is scoped to the named manifest and matches the scan: 0 declarers of the five; `name` 3, `label` 10, `description` 6, `data` 7, and each is still routed to `byName.get` (`validate.ts:240`). Two non-blocking imprecisions: the `Omit` sentence applies to every declared base attribute (a large regenerated-d.ts textual diff, type-equivalent), and "no new export" is not stated.
4. Prior FAIL fix 4 (vacuous `type` test): done. It is removed, with the reason at `:33-35`, and `type` is pinned through the list at `:54-56`.
5. Other surface: `SDUI_BASE_PROPS`, `SduiBaseProp` and `SduiBasePropScope` are module exports, unreachable from the package (`index.ts:11`; `package.json:8-14` maps only `.`). Accepted. `generateDts`'s `SduiBaseProps` goes from 8 to 19 members, with `Omit` for declared base attributes. Accepted as the port. `check:sdui-lockstep` still does not compare the list; that is the card's second question for the owning lane, not blocking.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: yes (widening)` with `minor` is consistent with AGENTS.md `:1084-1085`. The narrowing search, member by member, found no narrowed member: every declared pre-existing base attribute is equal or wider (`record:alert` `visible`), `children` is slot-only and untouched, and the eleven added members were never in the base before. An additional widening: the generated d.ts over the tracked manifest (`RecordAlertProps`, TS2430) now type-checks.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The dev did not read the prior record directly: no bearing; this head was verified against objectui directly.
- Two card comments, and the card's `done` report describes head `2ce8ceafbb`, now stale: a process gap; the PR body carries the correct state. No bearing on the verdict.
- The PR body was edited once and now describes the head accurately: no bearing.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20578-sdui-base-props-port`
Reviewed-by: `session_01VDtqoecgES7ScQYGbFVDRv`

**VERDICT: PASS**
